title: Governance DB Writer Authority Isolation and Readiness

phases.objective: Separate every reviewed Governance persistence mutation discovered by the DB privilege incident from the ordinary runtime DB identity, expose bounded effective-grant readiness before the first mutation, and make that readiness an effective Production runtime-parity blocker without live Production changes.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Capability envelopes, governed migration authorization, platform resource-authority grants, governed response chunks, runtime parity, and release readiness
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Runtime reads remain on the ordinary DB pool; reviewed governance mutations default to GOVERNANCE_DB_*; broad runtime pool injection cannot become write authority; effective privileges are evaluated against the exact table-scoped matrix with no raw grant or secret exposure; a recorded verified Production parity is downgraded to an effective degraded/blocked result whenever Governance DB writer authority is not ready; no Production DB, provider, migration, deployment, or protected-ref mutation occurs in this source slice.
steps: Resolve ordinary runtime authority and envelope lookups through the runtime read pool.
Resolve the Governance DB writer from mandatory GOVERNANCE_DB_USER and GOVERNANCE_DB_PASSWORD without DB_USER or DB_PASSWORD fallback.
Create, approve, and apply-authorize capability envelopes using the Governance writer.
Bootstrap governed migration authorization with separate readPool and writerPool roles.
Persist platform_resource_authority_bindings through the Governance writer, verify the inserted row on the writer, then verify visibility through the runtime reader.

Inspect and load governed response chunks through the runtime reader while persisting, extending TTL, deleting expired chunks, and performing immediate post-write verification through the Governance writer.
Probe CURRENT_USER(), DATABASE(), and SHOW GRANTS only through the Governance connection; normalize the result into the reviewed table/operation matrix without returning raw grants.

Fail readiness with runtime_db_write_authority_degraded when a required operation is absent, a broad/admin/DDL privilege is present, Governance configuration is missing, or the effective-grant probe fails.
Compose runtime parity with Governance DB readiness while preserving the persisted parity evidence as recorded_production_parity and recorded_blocking_gap_count.

Allow release readiness to keep its existing source contract and consume the effective runtime parity; verified Production therefore requires both zero persisted blockers and ready Governance DB write authority.
Publish the expanded least-privilege matrix including platform resource authority and governed response chunks.
Run synthetic regressions only; do not provision grants, secrets, Production, Migration 1050, Hostinger, provider, deployment, or restart mutations.
assertions: Governance username and password are mandatory and never fall back to runtime DB credentials.
A generic runtime pool cannot become lifecycle, resource-authority, or response-chunk mutation authority.
Resource-authority INSERT and first readback use the Governance writer; an independent runtime readback is also required.
Response-chunk schema/load reads use the read plane while INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and immediate integrity readback use the Governance writer.

The reviewed privilege matrix covers capability_resolution_envelope_ledger, approval_holds, governed migration registries/ledger, platform_resource_authority_bindings, and governed_tool_response_chunks.
DELETE is accepted only as the reviewed governed_tool_response_chunks cleanup operation, not as schema-wide authority.
Broad schema/global writes, ALL PRIVILEGES, GRANT OPTION, DDL, FILE, PROCESS, SUPER, and unreviewed table operations make readiness degraded.
Readiness exposes no raw SHOW GRANTS strings, password values, hashes, or credential fragments.
A persisted production_parity=verified result cannot remain effectively verified when Governance DB readiness is degraded.
Existing releaseReadiness.js source identity and static contracts remain intact; it continues to gate on the effective getRuntimeParity result.
No provider call or external business write is introduced by this boundary.

phases.objective: Provision and verify the least-privilege Governance DB principal and Production secret wiring after the expanded source repair is merged and promoted.
blockers: Dedicated MariaDB Governance writer principal has not been provisioned with the expanded table-scoped matrix.
Production GOVERNANCE_DB_USER and GOVERNANCE_DB_PASSWORD have not been configured and read back through a governed secret/configuration path.
Production promotion and runtime parity for this source repair have not been completed.
The bounded effective-grant readiness probe has not run against Production.

phases.objective: Prove missing credentials, insufficient grants, stale writer identity, transaction rollback, read/write pool misbinding, and broad privilege drift fail closed without runtime credential fallback.
No live DB canary is executed by this source-only PR.

Production remains blocked until exact-current-main promotion, least-privilege DB authority, secret configuration, runtime parity, effective-grant readiness, smoke persistence/readback, and a fresh Migration 1050 readiness authorization are completed independently.
blockers: Expanded source repair has not been merged and promoted through the normal main to Production lifecycle.
